texts: In Khaled Hosseini's novel "The Kite Runner," the main character, Amir, is approximately twelve years old at the beginning of the story. He lives in the city of Herat, Afghanistan, during his childhood before later moving to Chicago in the United States. The story explores his experiences growing up in a turbulent socio-political environment and his complicated friendship with Hassan, his half-brother and servant's son.

The Kite Runner follows Amir, who begins the story as a 12-year-old boy living in Kabul, Afghanistan, in the 1970s. He lives in a beautiful house in one of Kabul's wealthy neighborhoods with his father, Baba, who is a successful businessman and well-respected member of their community. The story follows Amir through different stages of his life, eventually showing him as an adult who immigrates to America during Afghanistan's political turmoil.

After settling in California with his father in 1981, Amir attends college at Berkeley and eventually becomes a published novelist. By the end of the novel, when he returns to Afghanistan to redeem himself for his past actions, he is in his late thirties. During this period, he travels through the war-torn streets of Kabul under the governance of the Northern Alliance, who had maintained relative stability in the region since 1996, allowing many Afghan expatriates to safely return to their homeland to reunite with family members.

In The Kite Runner by Khaled Hosseini, the main character, Amir, is approximately 29 years old at the start of the novel. He lives in Fremont, New Jersey, but was originally from Herat, Afghanistan before moving to the United States with his father, Baba.
